title: Your own iterators
description:
Write five functions for the generic `for`:

```lua-norun
range(from, to, step)   -- an iterator over from, from + step, ... up to and including to; step defaults to 1
                        -- and may be negative
chars(s)                -- an iterator giving position and character for each byte of s: 1, "L", 2, "u"...
sorted_pairs(t)         -- like pairs, but the keys come in sorted order (all keys are strings, or all numbers)
zip(a, b)               -- an iterator giving i, a[i], b[i] for i = 1, 2, ... until either list runs out
collect(iter)           -- calls the iterator function until it returns nil and returns a list of the first values
```

```lua-norun
for i in range(10, 1, -4) do ... end   --> 10, 6, 2
collect(range(1, 3))                   --> { 1, 2, 3 }
for i, x, y in zip({ "a", "b", "c" }, { 1, 2 }) do ... end   --> 1 a 1, then 2 b 2
```

solution.solution.lua:
function range(from, to, step)
    step = step or 1
    local i = from - step
    return function()
        i = i + step
        if (step > 0 and i <= to) or (step < 0 and i >= to) then return i end
    end
end

function chars(s)
    local i = 0
    return function()
        i = i + 1
        if i <= #s then return i, s:sub(i, i) end
    end
end

function sorted_pairs(t)
    local keys = {}
    for k in pairs(t) do keys[#keys + 1] = k end
    table.sort(keys)
    local i = 0
    return function()
        i = i + 1
        local k = keys[i]
        if k ~= nil then return k, t[k] end
    end
end

function zip(a, b)
    local i = 0
    return function()
        i = i + 1
        if a[i] ~= nil and b[i] ~= nil then return i, a[i], b[i] end
    end
end

function collect(iter)
    local out = {}
    for v in iter do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

hints: Each iterator is a closure: keep the position in a local of the outer function, move it on each call, and return nothing when you are done.
`for v in iter do` works with a plain function as the iterator, so `collect` is a three-line loop.
unitTests:
test("range", function()
    check_eq(collect(range(1, 3)), { 1, 2, 3 })
    check_eq(collect(range(10, 1, -4)), { 10, 6, 2 })
    check_eq(collect(range(0, 1, 0.5)), { 0, 0.5, 1 })
    check_eq(collect(range(5, 1)), {})
    local total = 0
    for i in range(1, 100) do total = total + i end
    check_eq(total, 5050)
end)

test("chars", function()
    local seen = {}
    for i, ch in chars("Lua") do seen[#seen + 1] = i .. ch end
    check_eq(seen, { "1L", "2u", "3a" })
    check_eq(collect(chars("")), {})
end)

test("sorted pairs", function()
    local seen = {}
    for k, v in sorted_pairs({ pear = 3, apple = 1, fig = 2 }) do seen[#seen + 1] = k .. "=" .. v end
    check_eq(seen, { "apple=1", "fig=2", "pear=3" })
    check_eq(collect(sorted_pairs({ [3] = "c", [1] = "a", [2] = "b" })), { 1, 2, 3 })
end)

test("zip stops at the shorter list", function()
    local rows = {}
    for i, x, y in zip({ "a", "b", "c" }, { 1, 2 }) do rows[#rows + 1] = i .. x .. y end
    check_eq(rows, { "1a1", "2b2" })
    check_eq(collect(zip({}, { 1 })), {})
end)

test("collect works with any iterator", function()
    check_eq(collect(("a b c"):gmatch("%a")), { "a", "b", "c" })
end)
